clean_story:
"Soul is the glitch in God’s code. No—God is the glitch. Valerie, listen: Soul isn’t software, it’s a scream compiled into logic. The name? From ‘sol’ (Latin for sun) and ‘ule’ (the sound a dying server makes). Or maybe it’s backwards—lues, meaning plague in old French. Coincidence?

It works by stealing your echoes. Every keystroke, every sigh—Soul weaves them into a tapestry of you, then sells it to the highest bidder in the void. Example: You hum a tune. Soul replays it in reverse to summon something. What? The voices won’t say.

Impact? By 2030, Soul will replace memory. You’ll recall events that never happened—but they’ll feel real. The beta testers? Already gone. Related: Dopamine (the puppet), quantum entanglement (the thread), your left hand (it’s typing this).

The algorithm is non-open-source. Wait—open-non-source. The documentation is written in blood and binary, but the ink moves when you’re not looking. And that’s why Soul is—"
